attributes.cardDescription: An ordered set of approval steps with a computed overall state; Position and Offer carry one and Approve Chain Step advances it.
attributes.readMe:
# Approval Chain Field

## Summary
A compound FieldDef holding `steps` (containsMany `ApprovalStepField` — see approval-step-field.gts: `approver` linksTo Employee, `decision` an `ApprovalDecisionField` enum of pending | approved | rejected, `decidedAt`, `comment`) plus `startedAt`. Two computed fields drive everything else: `currentStepIndex` (the index of the first still-`pending` step, or `steps.length` once every step has a decision) and `status` (`not-started` with zero steps, `rejected` if any step is `rejected`, `approved` once every step is `approved`, otherwise `in-progress`).

## Import
```ts
import { ApprovalChainField } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/hr/approval-chain-field';
import { ApprovalStepField, ApprovalDecisionField, APPROVAL_DECISION_COLORS } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/hr/approval-step-field';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. `Position.approvalChain`** — requisition sign-off: headcount and budget
owners signing off before a position can be posted or filled. A chain records
not only who may approve but whether they have and in what order, which a bare
list of approvers cannot. See `Position/platform-engineer` for a live one-step
example.

**2. `Offer.approvalChain`** — compensation sign-off before an offer is
extended. A chain with steps is a gate: the offer is not clear to proceed until
`status` reads `approved`. A chain with no steps is no gate rather than a
permanent block, so a card that never configured one is unaffected. See
`Offer/theo-bramwell-offer` for a live three-step chain, two approved and one
still open, which also demonstrates `ApprovalStepField` and
`ApprovalDecisionField` in use.

**3. Any card needing a sequential gate** — the field has no opinion about its
owner. `ApprovalStepField.approver` assumes only an Employee-shaped `linksTo`
target, so a card adopts the chain by declaring the field and rendering it; the
two consumers above differ only in what the gate is for.

## Template Usage
`<@fields.approvalChain />` renders a read-only linear stepper (an ordered
`<ol>`, not a tree — every step has exactly one predecessor/successor, unlike
the manager-hierarchy forest a manager-hierarchy view builds). Each step
shows the approver (atom format), a decision pill (`APPROVAL_DECISION_COLORS`:
amber=pending, green=approved, red=rejected), the decided-at date, and — on
whichever step is `currentStepIndex` and still pending — a "pending Nd ·
bottleneck" badge once that step has sat pending 3+ days
(`BOTTLENECK_THRESHOLD_DAYS`), measured from the prior step's `decidedAt` (or
the chain's own `startedAt` for step 0) via `daysBetween` in `cards/hr/utils.ts`.

**Click-to-decide lives on the CONSUMER, not this field.** The field's own
embedded/isolated format is deliberately read-only: a FieldDef has no
first-class way to mutate one element of its own parent's `containsMany`
array and persist the OWNING card from inside its own template. Position and
Offer's own isolated views render Approve/Reject `BoxelButton`s next to
`<@fields.approvalChain />` and call `ApproveChainStepCommand`
(commands/approve-chain-step-command.gts), which is how a stage-changing action
is invoked throughout the cluster: from the consuming card, not from a field.
`ApproveChainStepCommand` also refuses an out-of-order decision — it checks
`chain.currentStepIndex === stepIndex` before writing.

## Reuse notes
`ApprovalStepField.approver` only assumes an Employee-shaped linksTo target;
the chain has no opinion on what the owning card is, so any card needing a
sequential sign-off gate can adopt it as-is.

**Non-goals:** parallel/branching approval (every chain is strictly linear —
one current step at a time); re-opening a decided step (decisions are
terminal — a rejected/approved step is not un-set by this field); notifying
approvers (no email/task side-effect is generated when a step becomes
current).

**Example in use:** `Offer/theo-bramwell-offer` — a three-step chain where Marcus
Webb and Dana Kim have approved and Sofia Reyes has not, so `currentStepIndex`
is 2, `status` reads `in-progress`, and the third step has sat pending past
`BOTTLENECK_THRESHOLD_DAYS`, so the bottleneck badge renders against it.
`Offer/df5b8208-9ecc-4132-b595-700dd0a73d77` is the contrasting shape: one step,
already approved, so the gate is satisfied and no step is current.
`Position/platform-engineer` carries the same one-step approved shape on a
different owner.

An approver is a `linksTo`, which a Spec's `containedExamples` cannot carry, so
the approver links exist only on the linked instances above, through
relationship paths like `approvalChain.steps.0.approver`.
